newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - mogas plummets, fuel and CFDs hol.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - mogas plummets, fuel and CFDs hol.

text.p: Gasoline swaps were knocked up to $8 a tonne lower on Friday as NYMEX crashed through support levels. Naphtha was also lower, but fuel and Brent CFDs were steady to firmer.

Heavy fuel swap business was slowish with June concluded at 85.75, about $1 stronger than yesterday. Physical barges continued their mini-rally supported by continued short-covering buying which pumped prices up to $87.50.
Low sulphur fuel was also resisting crude's slide with June heard traded around $92.50/93.00.
Brent CFDs lost some of early day gains to rest fairly unchanged against Thursday. June 9-13 was pegged at -47/48 cents under July Brent, June 16-20 at -37/38 cents under July.

Dealers said June 16-20 was attracted a fair degree of dealing with -40 under July done, -38 done and -65 cents under August also done. Other dates saw June 9-13 concluded at -44 under July while June 9-20 went at July -40 cents.

Gasoline took a hamering with June swaps off $8 a tonne as the front month NYMEX contract plummeted to an 11-month low, crashing through support levels. A morning June trade was done at $198. By the day's close the number would have been closer to $195.
Dealers said there was more physical business than swaps, but July was done at $189 and $190. Physical barges were done around $200 for eurograde.

Naphtha also slewed lower with crude. Dealers were done around $184/184.50 for July before the screen lost ground while June traded at a touch under $184. Traders said swaps dropped about $1/1.50 from these levels once screen crude's slide began to bite.
